=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clearly visible paired leaves attached at the same node along the stem)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced out along the stem rather than tightly clustered)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (the structure consists of multiple leaflets attached to a central axis/rachis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (there is a distinct terminal leaflet at the end of the rachis)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 7 (visible on the most complete leaf structure)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): opposite (leaflets are paired along the rachis)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (smooth edges without teeth)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (widest in the middle and tapering at both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (tapering to a distinct point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base appears smooth and curved)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible and spaced, curving towards the margin
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (reflects light, indicating a smooth surface)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (surface appears smooth without visible hairs)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (leaflets are sessile or have very short attachment to the rachis)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (stem appears round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears rigid and lignified)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem appears smooth)
    19. Stem color: light brown
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (not visible in the images)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (not visible)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: Several leaves show damage in the form of irregular holes and missing tissue on the margins.
